item.title: [Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana] 2026 Osun Governorship Election: A Vote for Continuity or Change?Centre for Democracy & Development (CDD-West Africa)
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
2026 Osun Governorship Election: A Vote for Continuity or Change?Centre for Democracy & Development (CDD-West Africa)

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

This background paper examines the political, institutional and electoral dynamics shaping the 2026 Osun State Governorship Election, framed as a contest between continuity under incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party and change represented by Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Drawing on desk research, extensive media monitoring and key informant interviews, the report situates the election within Osun’s electoral history and assesses the factors likely to shape voter preferences across the state’s three senatorial districts.

The paper examines political incumbency, candidate identity, governance performance, intra- and inter-party realignments, influential political personalities, religious and traditional institutions, campaign narratives and voter mobilisation. It also highlights concerns around declining issue-based campaigning, political violence, vote trading, inclusion, electoral technology and public confidence in democratic institutions.

As the final governorship election to be conducted by INEC before Nigeria’s 2027 general elections, the Osun poll represents an important test of electoral preparedness, institutional neutrality and public trust. The report therefore calls for professional election administration, effective security, functional electoral technology, greater inclusion, sustained voter mobilisation and firm commitments by political actors to a peaceful and credible election.

item.content:encoded:
Operation Safe Corridor: What It Is and What It Is NotDan Woyengikuro Orufa

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

Boko Haram’s insurgency has caused deep harm across North-East Nigeria and the wider LakeChad Basin. For years, the Nigerian state has relied heavily on kinetic counter-insurgency operations, but military force alone has not ended the conflict.Operation Safe Corridor(OPSC) emerged as part of a non-kinetic response, designed to deradicalise, rehabilitate and reintegrate carefully screened low-risk associates of Boko Haram. Yet the programme remains widelymisunderstood. Much of the public concern results from a persistent communication problem: the programme has not been explained with enough clarity, consistency and sensitivity.

The central point that must be made clearer is that Operation Safe Corridor is not for every repentant Boko Haram member. It is designed for people categorised aslow riskafter screening and a prosecution process handled by the Ministry of Justice. In practical terms, low-risk participants often include people who were forcefully conscripted into Boko Haram, including farmers, fishermen and other local economic actors operating around the Lake Chad basin. They may also include civilians who were wrongly accused of terrorism because they lived in, passed through or traded within insurgent-controlled areas. Many of these people are better understood as victims of circumstance rather than committed ideological fighters.

item.content:encoded:
Benin's 2026 Vote: Insecurity, Political Re-engineering, and the Erosion of CompetitionCentre for Democracy & Development (CDD-West Africa)

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

Benin's 2026 presidential election marked the country's first democratic transfer of power since the political and constitutional reforms introduced under President Patrice Talon. Although the election was conducted peacefully and administratively efficiently, the overwhelming victory of the ruling coalition's candidate, Romuald Wadagni, with 94.05% of the vote raised important questions about the quality of political competition and the evolving character of Benin's democracy.

This report examines the political and security dynamics that shaped the 2026 election, arguing that its outcome cannot be understood solely through election-day processes. Instead, it situates the vote within a decade-long transformation of Benin's political landscape, characterised by constitutional and electoral reforms, shrinking civic and political space, judicial and institutional restructuring, and increasingly restrictive conditions for opposition participation. At the same time, the report analyses how escalating insecurity in northern Benin—driven by the southward expansion of jihadist groups from the Sahel—reshaped national political priorities, campaign narratives, and public expectations of the incoming administration.

item.content:encoded:
Centre for Energy and Climate Policy

发布源: IMANI Center for Policy and Education --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policyat IMANI is dedicated to finding lasting solutions to the persistent challenges in Ghana & Africa’s energy & climate sector. Despite numerous efforts to address the sector’s issues, progress has often fallen short due to a general lack of a comprehensive “follow through” approach. This underscores the need for remedial measures and their implementation to adopt a new direction and focus.

We believe that solving the energy & climate sector problems requires a multifaceted approach that includes thorough diagnosis of the sector’s issues, the development of innovative solutions, or the adoption of tried-and-tested remedial measures. Crucially, it also involves consistently tracking the implementation of these measures. This holistic approach informs our research and advocacy efforts at the Centre, ensuring that we contribute effectively to sustainable energy and climate policies in Ghana and across Africa.

Improving the Performance of State Actors in the Energy Sector-

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policy at IMANI Ghana assesses the performance of state actors in the energy sector. We evaluate public sector agencies responsible for energy based on key indicators such as transparency, efficiency, autonomy, and financial accountability. Through this comprehensive assessment, we aim to drive improvements and promote best practices within the sector, ensuring a sustainable and efficient energy landscape for Ghana and beyond.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
AN ANALYSIS OF THE GOVERNMENT OF GHANA’S 2026 MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW – POLICY BRIEF 26

发布源: Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

The mid-year budget review that was presented to Parliament on July 23, 2026, provided an opportunity for the government to report on the implementation of the 2026 budget, reassess the macroeconomic and fiscal outlooks for the year, and outline policy measures to support the realization of the government’s economic and fiscal objectives for 2026. This paper critically analyzes the review. Even though we find aspects of the review and the macroeconomic developments that are positive, we identify in this paper a number of important weaknesses about the review, which have undermined the credibility of the budget and the government’s ability to achieve its stated goals and objectives.

item.title: [Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana] INCREASING IMPORTATIONOF RICE IN GHANA: CAN THE COUNTRY TRANSFORM ITS FORTUNES IN THE RICE SECTOR?
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
INCREASING IMPORTATIONOF RICE IN GHANA: CAN THE COUNTRY TRANSFORM ITS FORTUNES IN THE RICE SECTOR?

发布源: Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-03

Importation of rice has been a serious issue of concern for the government of Ghana since the 1960s, due to its balance of payments, exchange rate, and food security implications. Therefore, over the years, the government has pursued a number of strategies to stem it. Yet, not only do data reveal that the strategies have failed to curtail it, they also reveal that rice importation has accelerated in recent years, making it assume alarming proportions.

This is because, even though the government is generally aware of the challenges facing the country’s rice sector, we find in this paper that the government’s strategies are not appropriate enough to address the fundamentals of the problem. Simply put, we find that there has been a policy failure in the country’s rice sector because the policies the government of Ghana has pursued in the sector are ill-suited. Methodologically, we have compared, in this paper, Ghana with Thailand and Vietnam, two major successful players in the global rice industry, in terms of the dynamics of rice import, production, and consumption.
